brief: AI-ecosystem anxiety (Fed tightening bets and government blocks on China chip access) drove a broad derisking: Nvidia led tech lower toward last week's lows after the company denied reports of Huang's return, NDX fell over 2.5% as the worst major index, NeoClouds were hit hardest, and IG, hyperscaler and data-center credit spreads widened (data-center CDS back above 450bps). Oil fell 2-3% despite Iran's tanker strikes in the Strait of Hormuz and drone attacks on a US base in Bahrain, because the IEA reported global supply exceeded demand for the first time since the conflict began, Goldman forecasts a 2mb/d glut into 2027, and a third US carrier group in the Gulf raises resolution odds, unwinding tail-risk premium; this pushed US retail diesel below $6, a first since September. Bonds stayed muted despite the selloff. Fed's Barr warned autonomous AI agents could accelerate bank runs; Warsh sees AI scenarios from productivity gains to labor disruption; Hammack favors smaller, steady hikes against broadening inflation. December hike odds fell while 2027 expectations rose, marginally hawkish, pushing the dollar to an 18-month high as crypto erased its post-August gains and gold slipped below October lows. Monkam says the 'Fed Put' looks absent, complicating dip-buying.
